panels.title: Live-sync subscribe outcomes/hour by topic class
panels.description: Multiplexed /ws/sync subscribe-authorization verdicts per topic class (REQ-FE-015, ADR-0094). A rising `denied` rate on a room every viewer should reach hints at an auth/gate regression; `allowed` includes transient fail-open.

panels.title: Live-sync subscriptions (live) by topic class
panels.description: Open /ws/sync topic subscriptions per topic class on this instance (basetool_livesync_subscriptions). The concurrent live-sync load denominator per surface; a flatline while sessions are active hints the socket or a room's subscribe is broken.

panels.title: Live-sync changed relay/hour by topic class
panels.description: Peer-forwarded `changed` frames per topic class (the per-surface breakdown of panel 28). A `changed` flatline on a surface whose viewers keep editing is the early indicator of the REQ-FE-010 stale-peer defect class.

panels.title: Redis fan-out pub/sub & errors/hour
panels.description: Cross-replica Redis fan-out for live delivery (ADR-0094/ADR-0126): the live-sync changed-relay (basetool_livesync_redis_*), the editor-presence gossip (basetool_livesync_presence_*) and the notification SSE fan-out (basetool_sse_redis_*). Publishing is fire-and-forget after the local relay/broadcast, so a rising `errors` stream means cross-replica delivery is silently degraded to single-instance — watched by the LiveSyncRedisFanoutBroken alert, which covers the changed relay and the SSE fan-out only (a lost changed frame costs correctness; a lost presence gossip costs a cosmetic dot, so it is a panel row, not a page). Note the presence rows are a PERIODIC gossip — one message per actively-edited topic per 10 s per replica — so a steady non-zero floor is normal there and a flat zero simply means nobody has a mission panel focused.

panels.title: Session evictions/hour
panels.description: Concurrent-session evictions (basetool_session_evicted_total): Spring Security expired a principal's oldest session because the per-user cap of 10 was full. The panel sits beside 'Active sessions' on purpose - the gauge cannot show this, because expireNow() only marks the session and leaves the registry entry and the Redis key in place. Rare by construction; a floor that never returns to zero means the registry is holding dead sessions against the cap and evicting live ones (watched by SessionEvictionSpike).

panels.title: Browser client errors/hour by kind
panels.description: Browser-side failures posted by the client error beacon (basetool_client_error_total, kind = script_error / unhandled_rejection / resource_error). A JS exception that kills a krtFetch handler issues no request at all, so it appears in no other panel on this dashboard. Read the shape, not the level: a low permanent background is normal (old browsers, extensions, tabs open across a deploy), a step in one kind that starts at a deploy and stays up is the broken live-update surface (watched by ClientErrorSpike).

panels.title: External catalogue fetch errors/hour by source
panels.description: Swallowed UEX / SC-Wiki fetch, parse and pagination-contract failures (basetool_external_fetch_errors_total). Each is mapped to an empty or incomplete result, so the sync job still records success and the staleness alerts stay quiet. For scwiki this doubles as the only proxy for 'the scwiki_deleted orphan sweep stood down this run': an incomplete page walk always contributes one increment here. A burst trips ExternalFetchErrors; a line that is non-zero on every daily run trips ScWikiCensusIncompleteStreak, which means orphan detection has been off for days.

panels.title: Ingest calls/hour by client
panels.description: Which client software is driving the ingest gateway (REQ-INGEST-011). The label is bounded by construction: an allowlist entry, or the literal 'other'. Traffic on 'other' means a caller whose azp is not on the allowlist - expected only while the gate runs in audit-only.

panels.title: Ingest client rejections/hour by reason
panels.description: Client-identity gate rejections (REQ-INGEST-011), also counted while audit-only is set. unknown_client / bad_provenance = an unapproved tool is calling the restricted interface. missing_azp / missing_scope = a Keycloak mapper or scope assignment regressed and the official extractor may be locked out. Backs the IngestUnknownClient alert.
